tier_reason: Public harness tests/bench.c (built by the Makefile's bench target) links the untouched qoi.h oracle at -O2 and at -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 with asm/qoi.asm in one binary, checks all outputs bit for bit before timing, and reports median TSC ticks and ns; the committed tests/bench_after_D1.txt matches every docs/BENCHMARKS.md row (1.07x-2.16x over -O3), on a named CPU (i7-14700F) with flags in the Makefile and gcc 13.3.0 shown by the .ident of the committed ref_asm/*.s files.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Baseline C is the untouched c/qoi.c, a two-line shim around c/qoi.h, which is byte-identical to phoboslab/qoi master qoi.h (sha256 7de6fca1a285b1c20d38f2723dec8b774eb9f144edb9710800a95feeea09375a, checked). Makefile: the -O3 baseline is gcc -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra followed by -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 (the later -O3 wins); the -O2 oracle is also timed; harness gcc -O2 -g; assembly via GNU as --64. The bench output does not print the compiler version; the committed ref_asm/qoi_O2.s and ref_asm/qoi_O3_x86v3.s carry .ident 'GCC: (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0', presumably the bench host's compiler. Reproduce with make bench BENCH_CMD='taskset -c 3 ./build/bench'.
corrections.caveats: Outputs are bit-identical to qoi.h: tests/bench.c compares ref -O2, -O3 and asm output bit for bit before timing (bench_after_D1.txt prints 'all encode/decode outputs bit-identical (ref == O3 == ASM)'), and the repo reports 19,185 differential cases plus ASan and UBSan runs. Drop-in for the qoi.h implementation: asm/qoi.asm exports the same four symbols (qoi_encode, qoi_decode, qoi_write, qoi_read) with the System V AMD64 ABI, so consumers keep the header and link qoi_asm.o or libqoi.a instead of defining QOI_IMPLEMENTATION; it needs x86-64-v3 (SIGILL on older CPUs) and does not run on non-x86 targets or the Windows x64 ABI. Weaknesses: single host under WSL2; all 7 inputs are generated by splitmix64-based fill functions in bench.c (random, 32x8 block runs, a 'photo-like' synthetic gradient plus noise, a 16-colour palette), not real photographs, and no qoibench corpus was used; cycles are invariant-TSC ticks that can understate core cycles by up to 2.4x, so only ratios and ns/op mean anything (run-to-run drift 6-8 percent); the three implementations run in a fixed order per row (C-O2, C-O3, ASM) rather than interleaved. Against the -O2 build of the same C, ASM is slower on one row (1080p_rgba_runs decode4: 2,299,300 vs 2,030,050 ticks, 0.88x, derived from page data), and the -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 build is slower than -O2 on several decode rows, so the 2.11x and 2.16x decode figures partly reflect an -O3 regression (vs -O2 those rows are 1.97x and 2.01x, derived from page data). The baseline is qoi.h, not libpng, libwebp or the other listed incumbents. README says it was produced by a multi-agent LLM workflow; the 'independent verifier' it mentions is part of that workflow. One commit, zero stars, published 2026-09-26, no outside reproduction.

notes: Harness, flags and result file check out; the oracle is byte-identical to upstream qoi.h and every BENCHMARKS.md ratio recomputes from tests/bench_after_D1.txt. Notability (0 stars, 1 commit, LLM-generated) and synthetic inputs are shortcomings, not grounds to reject; the one row slower than the -O2 C build is worth recording.

tier_reason: Issue #1 is a single informal comment (awesomebytes, 2022-07-24) giving 'about 20%' encode and 'about 30%' decode over qoixx on an i7-10875H, with no benchmark code, compiler, flags, qoixx version or repeat counts, and the repo has no benchmark; numbers without methodology are C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Issue #1 (2022-07-24, by awesomebytes, the author of the ROS PRs): 'About 20% faster to encode and about 30% faster to decode' than qoixx, 640x480 30 fps webcam stream, i7-10875H. ROS image_transport_plugins PRs #103 and #104 (same author, same day) state that they use libqoi and report, on the same i7-10875H, that QOI compression adds 28% CPU and decompression 13% CPU and keeps the 640x480 stream at 30 fps, while the existing PNG transport goes over 100% CPU and drops the stream to 3 fps.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 9 stars, 4 forks, 5 commits; used by ROS image_transport_plugins PR #103 (ROS 1, closed unmerged 2025-05-24 for Noetic end of life) and PR #104 (ROS 2, still open, unmerged)
corrections.caveats: One informal third-party comment: no benchmark code, compiler, flags, qoixx version, image content or repeat counts, and the stream is a live webcam so the numbers are end-to-end in a ROS node. The ROS PR #103 and #104 texts do name libqoi ('Dimitri Belopopsky's (@ShadowMitia) MIT Licensed library (https://github.com/ShadowMitia/libqoi)') as the library behind the 28%/13% CPU and 30 fps versus PNG's 3 fps figures, but those are CPU-load and frame-rate observations of a ROS transport plugin, not a throughput benchmark, and the PNG settings (compression level, encoder library) are not given; the PRs also quote the QOI format's general '20x-50x faster encoding and 3x-4x faster decoding' than PNG, which belongs to the format, not to this library. Neither PR was merged. No benchmark in the repo (tools/ holds only unix_compile.func). README calls it work in progress with expected API breaks. Last commit 2022-09-07.

notes: Record accurate apart from the claim that the ROS PR does not name its QOI library: PRs #103 and #104 both name libqoi, which adds a PNG-transport observation (30 vs 3 fps) to claimed_speedup but no methodology, so it stays C. Abandoned (last commit 2022-09-07, over 3 years).

tier_reason: README and UPSTREAM-CHANGES.md give first-party encode numbers against FFmpeg 8.1.2 palettegen/paletteuse (0.40-0.67x of its CPU time, PSNR +0.2 to +4.1 dB, 8 frames, 15 rounds), but the pinned ABBA harness, the frame corpus, the CPU, rustc flags and the FFmpeg build are not published; examples/encode_bench.rs times rusty_gif alone. First-party with partial methodology is C.

corrections.workload: Single-frame encode of 8 real-content frames (CIF to 1080p, corpus not published) with content-routed quantization (exact palette, frequency-weighted k-means over unique colours, or NeuQuant on a 125k-sample budget) versus FFmpeg 8.1.2's palettegen/paletteuse dither=none path; pinned CPU time, interleaved A/B, 15 rounds; quality gate is each output's PSNR against the source, which must exceed FFmpeg's PSNR on the same frame. Decode workload not described.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1 star, 0 forks, 6 commits; crates.io rusty_gif 0.1.0 (only version, 2026-08-12) with 874 downloads on 2026-10-04; the README banner's '874 active installs' equals that crates.io download count. README says it is the GIF codec of Remade-With-Rust/remade_ffmpeg_rs (rff).
corrections.caveats: The speedup comes from a cheaper quantizer, not a faster LZW coder: rusty_gif replaces FFmpeg's two-filter palettegen/paletteuse graph with its own census-routed quantizer, so the two arms do different work, and the quality side is judged by PSNR, which the k-means step is built to minimize (no perceptual metric, and dither=none on the FFmpeg side). Not reproducible from the repo: the pinned ABBA harness is referenced in UPSTREAM-CHANGES.md ('see repo bench notes') but is neither in this repo nor in remade_ffmpeg_rs (its readme and docs/benchmarks.md list GIF only as the pure-Rust gif crate, first frame, with no numbers); examples/ holds only encode_bench.rs (best-of-N wall time of rusty_gif alone, under the rusty_alloc-api 1.1.6 global allocator) and stage_profile.rs; CPU, compiler flags, FFmpeg build, thread settings and whether FFmpeg's CLI process time (input decode, filter graph, mux) was counted are not given. The decode claim ('up to 2.5x faster') has no numbers or workload, and UPSTREAM-CHANGES.md lists no decoder change (only vendoring color_quant, the census-routed quantizer, a NeuQuant contest() split and memoized palette mapping), so any decode speed belongs to upstream gif 0.14.2 with weezl. No comparison against giflib or the listed image-codec baselines. Performance fork of image-rs/image-gif (gif 0.14.2 plus color_quant 1.1.0), which has no benchmark data in its page. Rust, not C++. Part of Mata Network's Remade With Rust initiative; README opens with an install-count banner and an advert. Kept as a first-party claim, tier C.

notes: Record accurate; added the install-banner and crates.io match, the missing harness in remade_ffmpeg_rs as well, and that the decode claim has no fork-side decoder change behind it. Not a duplicate: remade_ffmpeg_rs is listed for its audio rows only, as with rusty_h265 and rusty_flac.
